theater: 萊茵河下游與北海沿岸

battle.name: 菲士蘭-法蘭克戰爭
battle.theater: 萊茵河下游與北海沿岸
battle.brief: 六〇〇年前後，墨洛溫王朝的法蘭克王國把矛鋒壓向萊茵河下游：渡河、攻壘、決堤，戰事夾在菲士蘭的堤丘與河口的商港之間，最後以菲士蘭王戰死與一批守軍淹斃在潮水裡收場。卡面這件亞述長矛早了一千五百年，是同類長兵的祖型；真正上陣的是墨洛溫短矛、投擲矛斧與圓盾。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是墨洛溫王朝的法蘭克王國，一方是北海沿岸的菲士蘭政權，兩邊的組織形態完全不同的樣子。法蘭克一方是萊茵河中下游幾個法區組成的聯盟式國家，國王的軍隊由薩利克法與里普阿里安法下的各個城區按份徵召，貴族以「得到土地的人」身分率部隨王出征，王室近侍與主教的武裝隨從構成骨幹；王權的軍事工具還有沿萊茵河與海岸線設置的堡式據點，第七世紀起由「海岸領主」分段接管，用以護衛河道、驛站與鹽場。菲士蘭一方則是海邊的堤丘聯盟：沿萊茵河口至威悉河之間的海岸被切成若干區，各區自有民兵、船隊與堤防，平日以漁汛、海關與海堤維生，遇戰則按區集結，由本區之王或首領率領。海馬的地理讓菲士蘭有一套別處沒有的防守辦法：他們能決口放水淹掉來軍腳下的泥灘，能在退潮時讓運兵的船隊擱淺，也能從堤丘背後的泥炭溝裡出奇兵。法蘭克這邊的難處，恰恰是敵人的地盤就是自己的補給線底盤：萊茵河下游的三角洲、鹽場與多雷斯塔德商港一旦被切斷，王室的戰費與漁獲稅就沒了來源。值得注意的是，這場戰爭裡雙方都不是純粹的外敵：七世紀末王位繼承危機中，奧斯特拉西亞的貴族普萊克特魯德曾聯合菲士蘭人反對克洛塔爾二世；法蘭克人自己也分成支持叛軍與支持王室的兩派。所以「菲士蘭人」在史料裡，有時是敵人，有時是盟友，而法蘭克王室的戰爭從來不是一條戰線。
countriesEn: The two parties were the Frankish kingdom of the Merovingian dynasty on one side and the Frisian polity of the North Sea coast on the other, and the two were organised in ways that bore no resemblance to each other. The Frankish side was a confederated state built on the river districts of the middle and lower Rhine; the king's host was mustered from the individual civitates of the Salic and Ripuarian law, nobles attended the king in person as men who had received land, and the household retainers and the armed retinues of the bishops formed its backbone. The military instruments of royal power also included the fortified posts set along the river and the shoreline, which from the seventh century were handed over in sections to the counts of the coast, to guard the waterways, the staging posts and the salt works. The Frisian side was a league of the sea dikes: the coast between the mouth of the Rhine and the Weser was divided into districts, each with its own levy, its own boats and its own embankments, living in normal times on the fishing tides, the customs and the dikes, and mustering by district when war came, under a king or a chief of their own. The geography of the sea gave the Frisians forms of defence found nowhere else: they could breach the dikes and flood the mud flats on which an attacking army had to stand, they could strand a transport fleet at low tide, and they could bring a sudden counter-stroke out of the peat cutting behind the terps. The difficulty on the Frankish side was precisely that the enemy's ground was the foundation of its own supply: once the delta of the lower Rhine, the salt pans and the emporium of Dorestad were cut off, the royal war chest and the fishery dues had no source. One further peculiarity is that the two sides were not always cleanly enemies: in the succession crisis at the end of the seventh century, Plectrud of Austrasia joined the Frisians against Chlothar II, and the Franks themselves split into a faction for the rebels and a faction for the king. In the sources, therefore, the Frisians are sometimes the enemy and sometimes the ally, and a Frankish war was never a single front.
people: 關鍵人物裡，最早成形的兩位，處在傳說與實史的交界處。菲士蘭王拉德博德是五世紀末最著名的對手：法蘭克王克洛維斯渡過萊茵、逼近巴達維時，他仍守著河口一帶的堡壘，退往海島方向，最後約在五〇五年前後死去；他死後，法蘭克人取得下萊茵與濱海一帶的統治權。進入中世紀編年史之後，出現一位王叫克洛迪奧，據《法蘭克人的事蹟》所記，他與菲士蘭人在布伊河一帶大戰，菲士蘭王阿瑟爾戰死，菲士蘭人的島上堡壘被攻破，金銀與王的器物被掠走；克洛迪奧其後醉死於萊茵河上的一座橋邊。史家多認為這段記載帶有明顯的傳說成分，但它是「法蘭克—菲士蘭」這條戰線最早的成文戰況。真正留下較硬細節的是七世紀的兩場：弗雷德加留斯《編年史》第四卷記克洛塔爾與其子多戈貝爾遠征反叛的菲士蘭人，菲士蘭王弗雷多戰死，許多人隨海潮淹死；「梅滕前編年史」也把弗雷多之死繫於七世紀三十至四十年代。稍後還有奧斯特拉西亞公爵普萊克特魯德，他以菲士蘭人為援軍起兵反對克洛塔爾二世，兵敗被殺，七世紀的記載把這一役寫成法蘭克人與菲士蘭人的正面衝突。第八世紀另有菲士蘭貴族巴杜赫爾姆在卡爾·馬泰爾時期叛變被誅，與七三四年博恩河之戰同屬一串餘波。信仰方面，傳教士威利布羅德於七世紀末到八世紀初在菲士蘭沿岸建立教區，足見戰爭的另一面是教會的推進。
peopleEn: The key figures belong to the seam where legend and recorded history meet. The earliest and best known is Radbod, king of the Frisians in the late fifth century: when Clovis crossed the Rhine and closed on Batavia, he still held the strongholds around the mouth of the river, withdrew towards the sea, and died around the year 505; after his death the Franks took control of the lower Rhine and of the coastal strip. Later in the medieval chronicles there appears a king called Chlodio, who in the Gesta Francorum is said to have fought a great battle against the Frisians at the river Bui, where the Frisian king Asser was killed and the island fortress of the Frisians was stormed, its gold, its silver and the regalia of the king carried off; Chlodio was afterwards killed in drunkenness at a bridge over the Rhine. Historians treat a good deal of this as legend, but it is the earliest written account of the Frankish and Frisian line of fighting. The details that survive better are the two episodes of the seventh century: the fourth book of Fredegarius' Chronicle records Chlothar and his son Dagobert marching against the rebellious Frisians, the Frisian king Fredo falling in the fighting and many men drowning as the tide came in; the Annales Mettenses priores likewise place the death of Fredo in the fourth decade of the seventh century. A little later comes Plectrud, duke of Austrasia, who rose against Chlothar II with Frisian auxiliaries, was defeated and killed, and the seventh-century sources write the episode as a clash between Franks and Frisians. In the eighth century the Frisian magnate Baduhelm rebelled in the time of Charles Martel and was executed, in the same sequence as the battle on the Boarn in 734. On the religious side, the missionary Willibrord established a diocese on the Frisian coast at the turn of the eighth century, which shows the other face of the war, the advance of the church.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛，要先講清楚它同本役的關係：它造於公元前九百年左右，短柄、長刃、鐵鏃，是兩河流域城邦軍隊的標準長兵；六〇〇年的萊茵河口不會有亞述長矛，戰場上也不會有，它屬於遠早於本役的年代卡。真正決定這場戰爭的兵器，是兩河流域長兵譜系在北歐的後代：從青銅時代的短柄長刃矛，到鐵器時代塞爾特與日耳曼人普遍使用的套筒鐵矛，再到墨洛溫時期法蘭克步兵的短矛，長約一點六至二公尺，握在盾後的矛列裡，以及柄約兩公尺、刃狹長的投擲矛斧，用來在盾牆前清出空隙。防具方面，菲士蘭堤丘墓葬出土的七世紀鐵鏈甲與脊飾盔顯示，這一帶的裝備水平與法蘭克騎士相當；法蘭克方還有薩拉米長劍、柄端單刃的短刀與投擲斧。盾是最關鍵的裝備：法蘭克圓盾直徑約四十至五十公分，鐵製盾臍與邊緣加固，數百人級的盾牆在正面形成可以承受矛陣衝撞的連續壁面；菲士蘭人則在堤丘上把盾牆用在塹壕與土壘背後。攻城方面沒有重型投射器械，兩邊都靠決堤改道、水淹與夜襲破壞，菲士蘭人的海上船隊還用來切斷法蘭克兵的糧道。補給線是法蘭克軍隊的弱點：從王都到戰場靠萊茵河船運與陸路車隊，攻到海岸後就地徵用漁獲與穀物；菲士蘭方面的物資來自海鹽、魚汛與琥珀。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card needs its relation to this campaign stated plainly first: it was made around 900 BC, with a short haft, a long blade and an iron head, and it was the standard long weapon of the city-states of Mesopotamia; there was no Assyrian spear of any kind at the mouth of the Rhine in the year 600, and none could be present on the battlefield, because the card belongs to a period far earlier than the campaign. The weapons that really decided this war are the descendants, in northern Europe, of the long arms of the Mesopotamian line: from the short-hafted blade spear of the Bronze Age, through the socketed iron spear used by Celts and Germans throughout the Iron Age, down to the short spear of the Frankish foot in the Merovingian period, roughly one point six to two metres long, carried in the spear line behind the shields, and the thrown spear-axe with a narrow blade and a haft of about two metres, used to clear a gap in front of the shield wall. On the defensive side, the mail and the spangenhelm recovered from seventh-century terp burials in Frisia show that the equipment level on this coast matched that of the Frankish warrior; the Franks also had the Salic long sword, the single-edged knife and the throwing axe. The shield was the decisive item: the Frankish round shield, roughly forty to fifty centimetres across, with an iron boss and a reinforced rim, allowed a formation of several hundred men to form a continuous wall on the front that could absorb the impact of a spear formation; the Frisians used their shields behind the ditch of a terp, backed by the earth rampart and the wooden palisade. There were no heavy missile engines of any kind: both sides relied on breaching dikes, on flooding and on night attacks, and the Frisian squadrons used their boats to cut the supply road of the Frankish army. Supply was the weak point of the Frankish host: from the royal centres to the theatre everything moved by Rhine boat and by wagon, and once the army stood on the coast it lived on what it could requisition in fish and grain; the Frisians drew theirs from sea salt, from the fishing tides and from amber.
tactics: 這場戰爭的骨架是水與土。開春萊茵河漲水、沼澤未退時不宜動兵，因此遠征多在五月至九月之間；過了秋天，海潮與泥灘又讓騎兵與車隊寸步難行，戰役的窗口一年只有幾個月。法蘭克軍隊沿萊茵河而下，補給靠河船，人員與戰具在下游城鎮集結後，或陸路、或乘內河駁船分批上岸；抵達海岸後先攻擊菲士蘭的堤丘：外壕挖在泥炭溝上，壕後是夯土斜坡，坡上立木柵，柵後才是住屋與倉房。攻方常靠人多同時壓上數處，或在夜裡沿已決口的水道摸進塹壕；守方的回應是放水淹灘、把進攻隊引入泥地，再以弓手與短矛從柵後消耗攻軍。若法蘭克人攻的是河口沙洲上的堡壘，菲士蘭人可以靠潮汐選擇攻守時機：退潮時堡外露出硬地，進攻者可以接近；漲潮時堡外成水，法蘭克人反而被困在泥裡，皮靴與弓弦都受潮，攻勢瓦解。另一個要點是雙方騎兵的用法不同：法蘭克騎兵人數不多，多擔任追擊與警戒，任務是截斷潰退的菲士蘭人；菲士蘭的輕騎與小船隊更擅長在退潮時切斷法蘭克軍隊的連絡線。戰局一旦對菲士蘭不利，結果多半不是全軍覆沒，而是「王死、眾散、堤被決」三件事同時發生：這正是弗雷德加留斯對這場戰爭的記錄方式。
tacticsEn: The skeleton of this war was water and earth. Nothing could be attempted in early spring, when the Rhine was in flood and the marshes were still impassable, so the expeditions were generally mounted between May and September; after autumn the tides and the mud flats again stopped cavalry and wagons in their tracks, and the window for campaigning was a few months in each year. The Frankish host moved down the Rhine, provisioned by river boat, the men and the equipment assembled in the lower towns and then landed either overland or from river barges in detachments; on reaching the coast they went after the terps: the outer ditch was cut across a peat cutting, behind it came a packed earth slope, on the slope stood a wooden palisade, and behind the palisade lay the houses and the storehouses. The attacker usually brought weight to several points at once, or crept in at night along a breach already opened in the water line; the reply of the defenders was to flood the flats, to draw the assault into the mud and then to wear it down with javelins and short spears from behind the palisade. If the Franks attacked a fortress on a sandbank at the mouth of the river, the Frisians could choose the moment of the tide: at low water firm ground was exposed outside the walls and the attacker could close; at high water the ground outside was water, the Franks were caught in the mud, boots and bowstrings took the damp, and the assault came apart. A second point concerns the different use of cavalry on the two sides: the Frankish horsemen were few and were employed for pursuit and for screening, their task being to cut off the Frisians as they broke; the light Frisian horse and the small boats were better at cutting the Frankish line of communication during the ebb. When a battle went against the Frisians, the result was rarely the destruction of the whole force: three things happened together, the king died, the host scattered, and the dikes were breached. That is the way Fredegarius records the outcome of this war.
data: 關於數字，得先老實說明這場戰爭的記載有多薄。編年史幾乎不給兵力數：提到大軍只寫眾多，提到慘敗只寫淹死甚多與王死；唯一帶有姓名的損失是菲士蘭王弗雷多戰死與阿瑟爾戰死。可用的硬資料有三類。第一類是法制的年表：里普阿里安法約在五一〇至五四〇年間成形，其中明白列出菲士蘭人與法蘭克人同受該法約束，這說明法蘭克王權在六世紀已把沿海的部分區域收編為法律上的臣屬，而不是只靠一次遠征。第二類是考古與地理：萊茵河自阿爾卑斯山麓到三角洲約九百公里，河口到威悉河口的海岸線約二百公里；多雷斯塔德位於萊茵河分汊處，七至八世紀的考古顯示當時有帶圍牆的大型商人群落與大片倉房，說明戰役爭奪的正是可控河的商路樞紐；荷蘭境內的堤丘土丘經數百年累積，多數高出周邊沼地二至五米，最高一處常被認為在維爾登一帶，堆土可達五米以上，這就是菲士蘭人守得住的原因。第三類是後世編年史的系年：克洛塔爾與多戈貝爾征菲士蘭人的一役，編年史繫於七世紀中葉，梅滕前編年史把弗雷多之死繫在七世紀三十至四十年代，另有系年把它提前到六〇〇年前後，本站年份即取這個傳統錨點；因此開戰月份只能按早期中世紀征戰多在春汛之後的慣例定為五月，並非史料所載。
dataEn: On numbers, it is best to be honest about how thin the record is. The chronicles give almost no figures for the armies: a great host is called numerous, a great defeat is recorded as many drowned and a king dead; the only named losses are the deaths of the Frisian kings Fredo and Asser. Three kinds of hard material are available. The first is the chronology of the law codes: the Lex Ribuaria, drawn up roughly between 510 and 540, names the Frisians among the peoples bound by it alongside the Franks, which shows that already in the sixth century royal Frankish authority had enrolled parts of the coastal zone as legal subjects rather than holding it only by an occasional expedition. The second is archaeology and geography: the Rhine runs some nine hundred kilometres from the Alpine foothills to the delta, and the coast from the river mouth to the mouth of the Weser is about two hundred kilometres; Dorestad stands at the branching of the Rhine, and seventh- and eighth-century excavation has shown a large walled trading settlement and extensive storehouses, which shows that what the campaigns fought over was the hinge of a navigable river; the terp mounds in the Netherlands, raised over centuries, stand mostly two to five metres above the surrounding marsh, and the highest, commonly placed at Wierden, exceeds five metres, which is why the Frisians could hold at all. The third is the dating of the later chronicles: the campaign of Chlothar and Dagobert against the Frisians is put in the middle of the seventh century by the Chronicle, the Annales Mettenses priores place the death of Fredo in the fourth decade of the seventh century, and other reckonings move it back to around the year 600; the year used here follows that traditional anchor, and the opening month can only be set by the general practice of the early Middle Ages, that expeditions went out after the spring flood, which makes it May, and not by anything the sources record.
cause: 打起上來有幾層原因。最表層是地盤：法蘭克人從萊茵河中游向右岸與下游擴張，第一個擋路的正是控制整個河口三角洲的菲士蘭政權；王國要在下游維持堡與稅站，菲士蘭人就要面對一條逐步逼近的界線。第二層是利益：河口一帶的商港多雷斯塔德是通往不列顛與北歐的轉口點，漁汛、鹽、琥珀與穀物都經過這片水域，誰掌握河道與堤防，誰就掌握稅關與航路；法蘭克王室的戰費開支正靠這條線，而菲士蘭人從裡頭取走的份額與拒絕的貢賦，就是衝突的實際內容。第三層是制度：法蘭克王權沿用羅馬的稅制與行政框架，對沿海的態度是要麼編入里普阿里安法下的臣屬名單，要麼照舊自治；菲士蘭人的村社在六、七世紀之交並不願意放棄選舉產生了王與首領的做法，於是在被征服與被編入之間長期拉鋸。第四層是法蘭克內部的裂痕：王位繼承與內戰使法蘭克一方屢屢自相殘殺，菲士蘭人懂得利用這一點，與反對在位的奧斯特拉西亞派聯合，使自己成為法蘭克內政的變數。最後還有信仰：墨洛溫王朝自克洛維斯受洗之後以基督教立國，菲士蘭沿岸仍維持北歐的古老信仰，傳教士與修道院在堤丘上建堂修院，等於同時在劃界，戰爭與傳教並行，這也是七世紀末威利布羅德能在菲士蘭海岸建立教區的原因。
causeEn: There were several layers of cause. The most obvious is ground: as the Franks expanded to the right bank and downstream of the Rhine, the first power in the way was the Frisian polity, which controlled the whole delta of the mouth; the kingdom had to hold posts and levy stations downstream, and the Frisians faced a frontier that moved closer every year. The second layer is interest: the emporium of Dorestad at the mouth was the transshipment point for Britain and for the north, and fish, salt, amber and grain all passed through these waters; whoever held the channels and the dikes held the customs and the shipping lanes, and the Frankish war chest was funded by exactly that line, while the share the Frisians took from it and the tribute they refused to pay were the substance of the quarrel. The third layer is institutional: Frankish kingship kept the tax system and the administrative frame of Rome, and its attitude to the coast was either to enroll the districts as subjects under the Ripuarian law or to leave them autonomous; the village communities of the Frisians were not willing, in the sixth and seventh centuries, to give up the practice of electing their king and their chiefs, so there was a long pull between being conquered and being enrolled. The fourth layer is the internal fracture of the Franks: succession disputes and civil war repeatedly set Franks against each other, and the Frisians understood how to use this, joining the Austrasian party opposed to the reigning king and making themselves a variable in Frankish politics. Last comes faith: the Merovingian kingdom had set itself up as Christian since the baptism of Clovis, while the Frisian coast still kept the older northern religion, and the mission stations and the monasteries built on the terps marked out a frontier at the same time as the armies did, so that war and evangelisation ran in parallel; that is how Willibrord could establish a diocese on the Frisian coast at the end of the seventh century.
impact: 這場戰爭沒有留下明確的條約，卻留下了一整套北歐的邊疆結構。首先是海岸區的設立：法蘭克王國在萊茵河口至威悉河之間設一段由海岸領主分段管治的邊區，第七世紀起由克洛塔爾二世時代的郡伯與第八世紀的巴杜赫爾姆先後掌管，其職責是守堤、護航、徵漁獲稅與護送鹽車；這段制度一直演到加洛林時期，成為荷蘭與德國北部沿海的行政底層。其次是軍隊的融合：菲士蘭人被打散編入法蘭克以及其後加洛林的軍隊，北方沿海的輕步兵與水兵從此是帝國常備兵的一部分，第八、九世紀加洛林擴張時，那些善於水戰的北方兵將屢見於戰役名錄。第三是教會與文字：堤丘上的木教堂升為石構，烏得勒支與威克比杜爾斯特德的教區成立，烏得勒支主教區日後成為北方教會的重心；古法蘭西語在沿海退隱，法蘭西語各方言的過渡被推後，同時古法蘭西語與古薩克森語在北部形成方言連續體，荷蘭語的方言地圖因而大致成立。第四是戰術與制度的最後一課：這場戰爭反覆證明，在堤丘與水網之地，能決定勝負的是堤、壕、船與潮，而不是任何單一件兵器；把戰爭記在矛兵身上，是後世詩人與編年史的取捨，不是戰場的實況。第五是對外貿易：多雷斯塔德的商人群落在戰後不但沒有衰落，反而在法蘭克保護下擴張，成為九至十世紀北海貿易的節點，菲士蘭人的航海技術與網絡，讓荷蘭海岸在往後數百年一直是歐洲北部的門戶。
impactEn: This war left no clear treaty behind, but it left behind a whole structure for the defence of the northern coasts. First came the creation of the coastal march: between the mouth of the Rhine and the Weser the Frankish kingdom set up a frontier district administered in sections by the counts of the coast, taken over from the time of Chlothar II in the seventh century and by Baduhelm in the eighth, whose duties were to hold the dikes, escort shipping, collect the fishery dues and guard the salt convoys; the arrangement ran on into the Carolingian period and became the administrative floor of the Dutch and the north German coast. Second, the fusion of the armies: the Frisians were broken up and incorporated into the Frankish and later Carolingian forces, and from then on the light infantry and the boat crews of the northern coast were part of the standing army of the empire, and the northern men skilled in fighting on water appear repeatedly in the rosters of the Carolingian wars of expansion. Third, church and script: the wooden churches on the terps were rebuilt in stone, the sees of Utrecht and of Wijk bij Duurstede were founded, and the diocese of Utrecht became the centre of the northern church; Old Frisian receded from the coast, the transition from Old Frankish to the Frankish dialects was postponed, and at the same time Old Frisian and Old Saxon formed a dialect continuum in the north, so that the dialect map of Dutch was in effect established. Fourth, the final lesson of tactics and institutions: this war demonstrated again and again that on ground made of dikes and water the outcome was settled by the dike, the ditch, the boat and the tide, and by no single weapon; to record the war as a war of spear men is the choice of later poets and chroniclers, not the condition of the field. Fifth, external trade: the trading settlement of Dorestad not only survived the war, it expanded under Frankish protection and became the hinge of North Sea trade in the ninth and tenth centuries, and the seamanship and the connections of the Frisians kept the Dutch coast the gateway of northern Europe for several centuries afterwards.
result: 打完之後，菲士蘭作為獨立王國不再存在。弗雷多戰死，堤丘上的守軍在退潮時被切斷、在漲潮時被淹，倖存者散入內陸的村社；多雷斯塔德與下游堡壘由法蘭克守軍接防，河流與航路由王室的海岸領主分段看守，菲士蘭人自此以臣屬的身分留在原地。這個結局並非一勞永逸：六八〇至六八三年，王位繼承內戰中菲士蘭人站在奧斯特拉西亞派一方，結果是普萊克特魯德兵敗被殺、菲士蘭人再受一次懲罰；七三四年博恩河一戰，菲士蘭軍隊被引入河中，殘部慘敗，巴杜赫爾姆被誅；七九二至七九三年的起事再度失敗，卡爾大帝把整個沿海地區收編為加洛林王國的一個郡，菲士蘭自由只剩下最北邊幾個奧姆蘭，名義上保留自治，實際上直到十三世紀才被黑森與荷蘭的伯爵逐步收編與劃界。宗教與法律也跟著落實：威利布羅德在七世紀末建立教區，加洛林時期頒布菲士蘭法，納稅與服役的形式保住，而制度的細節改掉。最後要回應卡面：這件亞述長矛確實沒有出現在六〇〇年的萊茵河口，它的作用是標示長兵譜系的上游，從兩河流域的短柄長刃矛，到塞爾特與日耳曼的套筒鐵矛，再到墨洛溫短矛與投擲矛斧，最後進入加洛林的密集矛列；而在本役裡，矛只是列陣的骨架，真正決定勝負的，是堤、潮與船，以及一批被潮水淹斃的守軍。
resultEn: When it was over, the Frisians no longer existed as an independent kingdom. Fredo was dead, the garrisons of the terps were cut off at low tide and drowned at high tide, and the survivors scattered into the villages of the interior; Dorestad and the forts below it were taken over by Frankish garrisons, the river and the shipping lanes were watched in sections by the counts of the coast, and the Frisians stayed where they were as subjects. That outcome was not final: in the civil war over the succession in 680 to 683 the Frisians stood on the side of the Austrasian party, and the result was the defeat and death of Plectrud and a fresh punishment of the Frisians; in the battle on the Boarn in 734 the Frisian army was drawn into the river, the survivors were destroyed, and Baduhelm was executed; the rising of 792 to 793 failed in turn, and Charles the Great incorporated the whole coastal region as a county of the Carolingian kingdom, while the Frisian freedom survived only in the most northerly Ommelanden, which kept a nominal autonomy in name and was gradually taken over and delimited by the counts of Hesse and Holland in the course of the thirteenth century. Religion and law settled at the same time: Willibrord established the diocese at the end of the seventh century, the Frisian law was issued under the Carolingians, and the form of taxation and service was preserved while the substance was changed. Finally, back to the card: this Assyrian spear really did not stand at the mouth of the Rhine in the year 600, and its function is to mark the upper end of the lineage of the long weapons, from the short-hafted blade spear of Mesopotamia through the socketed iron spear of the Celts and Germans to the Merovingian short spear and the thrown spear-axe and on into the dense spear lines of the Carolingians; and in this campaign the spear was only the frame of the formation, while what decided the outcome was the dike, the tide and the boat, and a garrison drowned by the incoming sea.
